name: webpack-resolve-fallback-node-false-does-not-handle-node-protocol
hook: resolve.fallback node:false does NOT handle node: protocol imports — need resolve.alias
body: webpack 5's resolve.fallback with { node: false } only handles BARE 'node' specifiers (e.g., require('node:console') is NOT bare, it uses the node: URI scheme). The node: protocol scheme requires resolve.alias to redirect — use '\.node$' for native binary files and '^node:(.*)$' for all node: protocol imports to an empty stub. resolve.fallback.node: false is a necessary supplement but not sufficient alone.
why: CI was failing with 'UnhandledSchemeError: Reading from node:crypto is not handled by plugins' even with resolve.fallback.node: false set. Adding resolve.alias with '^node:(.*)$' pattern fixed it.

name: next-config-js-uses-esm-require-unavailable
hook: next.config.js is ESM — use path.resolve not require.resolve
body: next.config.js uses ESM (import at top level), so require is not available. When adding webpack resolve.alias entries that need a file path, use path.resolve(process.cwd(), ...) instead of require.resolve(...). process.cwd() gives the project root at build time.
why: CI failed with 'ReferenceError: require is not defined' at next.config.js because the file is ESM but require was used in the webpack config callback.

name: serverexternalpackages-not-sufficient-for-canvas
hook: serverExternalPackages alone does not prevent webpack from analyzing @napi-rs/canvas
body: @napi-rs/canvas in serverExternalPackages (Next.js config level) is not sufficient to prevent webpack from analyzing the package at build time. Webpack still resolves the package's internal imports (including .node binaries and node: protocol imports). Must ALSO add '@napi-rs/canvas' to webpack externals (inside webpack config callback) to prevent webpack from processing it.
why: Even with @napi-rs/canvas in serverExternalPackages, CI still showed '@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-gnu/skia.linux-x64-gnu.node is not supported in the browser' errors. Adding it as a webpack external (string, not regex) fixed it.

name: minify-webpack-plugin-canvas-regex-externals-conflict
hook: Canvas regex externals (but not string externals) conflict with minify-webpack-plugin
body: Using '/^@napi-rs\/canvas-/' as a webpack external regex (with other regex externals) caused minify-webpack-plugin to fail with 'HookWebpackError: _webpack.WebpackError is not a constructor'. Using '@napi-rs/canvas' as a STRING external (not regex) avoids this conflict while still preventing webpack from bundling canvas.
why: The complex combination of regex externals (canvas + other patterns) produced an error state in webpack that minify-webpack-plugin couldn't serialize. Simplifying to string externals avoided the issue.

name: nextjs15-isServer-isNodeOrEdgeCompilation
hook: Next.js 15 webpack config: isServer is isNodeOrEdgeCompilation — use !isClient for non-server-only configs
body: In Next.js 15.5.9, the isServer parameter passed to the webpack config function is actually set to isNodeOrEdgeCompilation (isNodeServer || isEdgeServer), meaning isServer=true for BOTH Node server builds AND Edge builds. So 'if (!isServer)' is false for Edge builds, skipping the config. Use 'if (!isClient)' instead to correctly identify browser-only builds, allowing the config to also apply to Edge builds. isClient=true only for browser builds; false for both server and Edge.
why: CI was still failing with node:protocol and .node native binary errors. Using !isClient instead of !isServer ensures the webpack config applies to Edge builds as well as browser builds.
